aggregate_chart_policy._note: Hierarchy-generated aggregates are shown as a by-product/by-flow pair only when at least two immediate child flows carry non-zero data in a displayed dataset or scenario. Explicit leaf summaries such as Supply balance rows and Non-energy use remain available without invented child detail. Page-specific placeholder and balance-overview charts are configured separately and are therefore retained.

other_transformation_page._note: The Overview keeps transformation, residual own use, losses and transfers separate. Multi-flow summaries group by flow; single-flow summaries fall back to product, matching the Refining overview rule. Transformation detail stays disaggregated and is labelled as inclusive of auxiliary-fuel own use. Residual own-use rows already absorbed into an upstream inclusive Common ESTO boundary are excluded using upstream component and non-expanding-rollup contributor metadata, not a dashboard mapping list.

routing_special_cases.reason: Electricity and heat transmission/distribution losses belong with their Power generation and own-use boundary; all other 10.02 products remain on Other transformation.
Transfers are routing operations shown as their own section under Other transformation.
Exact flow 17 is presented as a Non-energy use section on the Industry page.
LEAP currently reports Other sector and non-energy as one inseparable aggregate; exact standalone code 17 is shown in the Industry page's Non-energy use section.

sector_pages.rule_note: Supply and top-level balancing rows, including signed international-transport bunkers. Matches generated labels by any component code, not just the first displayed code.
Electricity and heat output, plus directly related power-sector own-use rows. The specific 09.01/09.02 roots take ownership ahead of the broader Other transformation root 09.
Oil refining rows. The specific 09.07 root takes ownership ahead of the broader Other transformation root 09; transfers use an explicit routing special case.
Transformation, energy own-use, extraction own-use, and losses not owned by a more-specific Power or Refining root. Transfers use an explicit routing special case.
Domestic transport final energy demand rows.
Residential, commercial, public services, and datacentre rows.
Other final demand rows outside buildings/industry/transport.

total_demand_page.tfec_status: Enabled only when the source publishes a distinct non-energy-use branch; combined Other/non-energy placeholders are not allocated.
total_demand_page._note: supply_total = sum of signed values for codes 01 (Production), 02 (Imports), 03 (Exports), and the common 04-05 International transport (bunkers) comparison row. The combined bunker row is used in overview totals so its retained 04/05 source children are not counted again; the detailed children remain available on the Supply page. Bunkers are supply deductions and are excluded from domestic demand. Stock changes (06) remain outside the projection-comparable total. The transformation overview combines all flow-09 transformation sectors with flow 08 transfers, flow 10.01 energy-sector own use, and flow 10.02 transmission/distribution losses. Its by-flow areas use the deepest available non-overlapping flow nodes, while its net lines and by-fuel chart retain the authoritative whole-boundary frontier. Unmet Requirements remains a separate LEAP-only diagnostic: only its fuels are resolved to the selected Common ESTO category scope; positive values mean shortage and negative values mean surplus.

supply_page._note: Show international marine bunkers (04) and international aviation bunkers (05) separately on Supply whenever a displayed comparison source publishes both child boundaries with non-zero data. Resolve the additive bunker frontier independently for each source/scenario/year: a source with only the combined International transport value retains 04-05 for balance totals but is not allocated into, or plotted on, either exact child chart. When no displayed source has a complete 04/05 split, show one combined 04-05 placeholder. The combined row remains available to the Energy balance overview for its supply total. Stock changes and statistical discrepancy are balancing rows rather than projection series. Source their base-year fuel values from the ESTO and LEAP comparison scope, label the boundary explicitly, and exclude them from ordinary line and area charts. For Statistical discrepancy only, multiply LEAP chart values by -1 to align the displayed sign with ESTO; do not take absolute values and do not change the upstream comparison fact. Missing source values are unavailable, not zero.

emissions_page._note: The Emissions page contains exactly two charts: emissions by fuel and emissions by major sector. The original-ESTO-flow policy at flow_policy_path is the authority for whether a balance row is included in the factor-based combustion estimate; measured_in_dashboard does not mean the source contains directly measured emissions. Extended Common ESTO rows inherit the longest original ESTO ancestor, and mixed included/excluded rollups fail closed. Final demand is split into Industry, Transport, Buildings, and Other demand. Negative power-sector transformation inputs and separately reported 10.01 energy-sector own use are treated as combustion. Conversion feedstocks (including refining, LNG/gas processing, coal transformation, petrochemicals and hydrogen production), positive outputs, transfers and 10.02 transmission/distribution losses are excluded. Non-energy and mixed final-consumption aggregates are excluded. Sources with no sector detail may use aggregate_flow_code 13 Total final energy consumption, which excludes non-energy use, without inventing a sector split. Factors and their mapping axis live in factor_sets_config_path; leave factor_set_key empty to use the active factor set. frontier_coverage_tolerance_pj is the PJ gap above which the page warns that retained detail does not add back to a reported aggregate.

leap_demand_sector_coverage._note: page_leap_branches maps each domestic demand page_key to its LEAP source branches. The dashboard workflow resolves aggregate-only sectors from leap_mappings/config/all_demand_aggregated_components.json. A placeholder_only_retained component keeps its broad aggregate boundary but suppresses its by-product/by-flow detail cards and their otherwise-empty section navigation after routing; those cards return when the detailed LEAP branch replaces the placeholder. When every page_placeholder_components entry is placeholder-only, suppress that page's parent detail code too while preserving its overview. International transport is a signed supply deduction and is routed to Supply, not domestic demand. Exact flow 17 is presented in the Industry page's Non-energy use section; the combined Other sector including non-energy placeholder remains routed to Other demand by its explicit routing special case, so its active prefix set must also suppress routed 17 detail on Industry.

by_flow_overview.label: 16.03-16.05 Other sector
by_flow_overview.stacked_area_note: The historical areas show the activities included in Other demand. A projected combined category is shown as one activity only when the observed base-year data show that activity accounts for the full category; otherwise it remains combined until more detail is published.

other_demand_page._note: Both Other-demand Overview charts always use exact boundary 16.03-16.05; broad flow 16 is suppressed because it also contains sectors presented on the Buildings page. The by-flow source frontier retains a published 16.03-16.04 compound when a source does not publish its separate 16.03 and 16.04 children, then uses the deepest available non-overlapping detail. Any remaining parent/detail difference is shown conservatively as unallocated rather than assigned to a specific child. A source/year with no child detail retains its published parent unless exactly one historical child reconciles to the compound; the active LEAP placeholder is otherwise retained. Source-specific comparison rollups 16.03-16.04 and 16.03-16.05 are already owned by the continuous Overview and are not repeated below as misleading historical-only or projection-only detail sections.

buildings_page._note: The detailed Buildings Overview is deliberately limited to the complete Buildings boundary and its Services branch. Each is shown by fuel and by immediate child flow. The full Buildings view uses Commercial/public services plus Residential; the Services view uses Datacentres plus the explicitly unallocated Commercial/public-services remainder. Broader flow 16 and duplicate detail summaries are not shown.

aggregates.label: 09.01-09.02 Power
aggregates.stacked_area_note: Electricity, CHP and heat plant inputs and outputs are shown together. Interim plant placeholders contribute until detailed LEAP plant branches replace them.

grouping_titles.product: 10.02 Transmission and distribution losses — by product
grouping_titles.flow: 10.02 Transmission and distribution losses — by flow

power_page._note: Power Overview uses by-product summaries for active first-level boundaries and adds by-flow summaries when at least two immediate children are non-zero. Power, Electricity plants, CHP plants, Heat plants, and transmission/distribution losses are separate navigation owners; process children remain below their plant boundary.

placeholder_navigation._note: Demand placeholder navigation is driven by the current-run representation audit and placeholder_component_product_sections. Power status comes from the source-branch fallback audit. Each retained interim branch maps to one explicit Common ESTO plant roll-up; fuel-specific CHP children and 10.01.01 own use are not placeholder identities. A configured owner is shown only when its interim branch is retained and mapped comparison rows exist.

section_aggregate_overrides._note: A section override with required_flow_boundary filters its aggregate to that boundary. The Transport override removes the redundant generic by-product section summary once Road is detailed, keeps its technology/flow summary strictly within 15.02, relabels it as Road detail, and places it first inside the existing Road-owned by-product section. This produces one Road navigation chip and one destination while non-road remains owned by its separate overview. The Power override hides only the misleading residual own-use/storage section summary because the complete Power-sector aggregation is owned by Overview; its useful detailed cards remain below.

power_interim_branch_flow_prefixes._note: When an interim branch is retained in the upstream fallback audit, hide its Power detail cards. The page-level Power aggregates remain until each interim branch is replaced by its completed LEAP source branch.

scope_specific_pages._note: Optional diagnostic alternate-scope pages. Keep disabled by default until each page has been reviewed for production usefulness; when enabled, pages are generated only when matching rows exist in the input data.

pages.page_note: Diagnostic LEAP vs 9th transport detail. This view can include sparse alternate-scope rows that are not suitable for the default dashboard until reviewed.
Diagnostic LEAP vs 9th datacentre demand detail. This view is hidden by default because current fixtures expose only sparse alternate-scope rows.

secondary_pages._note: No secondary pages are published. International marine and aviation bunkers remain on Supply and in TPES without a duplicate International transport page.

sankey_diagrams._note: Sankey generation is intentionally disabled until balance-routing rules define how signed common ESTO flows connect without double-counting.
